{{Short description|Mathematical theorem}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''theorem of absolute (cohomological) purity''' is an important theorem in the theory of [[étale cohomology]]. It states:<ref>A version of the theorem is stated at {{cite arXiv|last=Déglise|first=Frédéric|last2=Fasel|first2=Jean|last3=Jin|first3=Fangzhou|last4=Khan|first4=Adeel|date=2019-02-06|title=Borel isomorphism and absolute purity|eprint=1902.02055|class=math.AG}}</ref> given
*a [[regular scheme]] ''X'' over some base scheme,
*<math>i: Z \to X</math> a [[closed immersion]] of a regular scheme of pure codimension ''r'',
*an integer ''n'' that is invertible on the base scheme,
*<math>\mathcal{F}</math> a locally constant étale sheaf with finite stalks and values in <math>\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}</math>,
for each integer <math>m \ge 0</math>, the map
:<math>\operatorname{H}^m(Z_{\text{ét}}; \mathcal{F}) \to \operatorname{H}^{m+2r}_Z(X_{\text{ét}}; \mathcal{F}(r))</math>
is bijective, where the map is induced by cup product with <math>c_r(Z)</math>.

The theorem was introduced in SGA 5 Exposé I, § 3.1.4. as an open problem. Later, [[Robert Wayne Thomason|Thomason]] proved it for large ''n'' and [[Ofer Gabber|Gabber]] in general.<!-- true but provide more historical context before mentioning this: The theorem is used as a key ingredient in the study of Chern classes of a closed immersion of a regular scheme. -->
